reviewer: Codex assistant; qualitative inspection, not independent human gold
scope: Ten selected examples across four routes; no parser-accuracy score is derived.

cases.title: Landing roles and name
cases.requirement: IM-1 is the lander; the moon is its location. Retain the past tense.

assessments.srl: The trained SRL preserves IM-1 as ARG1 and on the moon as a location phrase. The location phrase is not internally decomposed.
assessments.amr: land-01 has ARG1=IM-1 and location=moon. The source-aligned temporal atom is past/simple.
assessments.direct: The graph assigns ARG0=IM-1 and ARG1=moon. This is the wrong PropBank land-01 frame even though the compiler accepts it.
assessments.guided: Dependency/SRL assistance still produces ARG0=IM-1 and ARG1=moon. Assistance did not preserve the supplied semantic roles.

cases.title: Passive patient and polarity
cases.requirement: Shi Yongxin is the person arrested; the claim has no overt arresting agent or negation. Preserve perfect aspect.

assessments.srl: ARG1=Shi Yongxin; no agent is invented. The auxiliary chain supplies present/perfect.
assessments.amr: arrest-01 ARG1=Shi Yongxin; no agent is invented. The auxiliary chain supplies present/perfect.
assessments.direct: Assigns the arrested person to ARG0, the arresting agent. The program is executable but the role is wrong.
assessments.guided: Assigns Shi Yongxin to ARG0 and adds negative polarity to a positive sentence. This is an incorrect accepted translation.

cases.title: Written source scope
cases.requirement: The text asserts a death-toll claim. Do not assert actual deaths or the toll as unscoped world facts.

assessments.srl: The adapter was revised after inspection: read-01 uses ARG1 for Text and ARG3 for the content. The inner reach frame is excluded from world assertions. Content remains one proposition.
assessments.amr: The pretrained graph uses ARG1=text and ARG3=content. The revised frame-specific compiler preserves OCR scope; inner cause/die/reach predicates are not asserted as world facts.
assessments.direct: Reuses graph variables for different concepts; refused. Its attempted content graph also changes the structure of the quoted text.
assessments.guided: Reuses graph variables for different concepts; refused. No semantic success is claimed for this output.

cases.title: Depiction and embedded content
cases.requirement: Photos depict buildings in a collapsed state. Preserve that content inside the photo scope.

assessments.srl: Preserves the exact collapsed buildings phrase as photo content; it does not separately compile building/collapse relationships.
assessments.amr: Preserves building and collapse inside a reified photo-content graph; no unscoped collapse assertion. Internal content is not yet recursively compiled.
assessments.direct: Preserves an attempted building/collapse content graph under the photo. Internal content is opaque to the current executable program.
assessments.guided: Preserves a collapsed-building content graph under show. Internal content is opaque to the current executable program.

cases.title: Lexical meaning and direction
cases.requirement: Haboob denotes the moving phenomenon, approaching an airport. Do not silently turn it into a city.

assessments.srl: Keeps Haboob and towards airport as argument phrases. This preserves wording but leaves lexical typing and internal direction decomposition unresolved.
assessments.amr: Incorrectly types Haboob as a city name. The compiler retains that city condition; executable output does not correct the lexical error.
assessments.direct: Retains a haboob concept but uses an unvalidated come-01 role frame. Direction is not explicitly distinguished from its airport argument.
assessments.guided: Retains a haboob concept but separates towards from airport into different arguments. The intended direction/target relation is not cleanly represented.

cases.title: Modifier attachment and untranslated edges
cases.requirement: The Alaskan qualifier applies to the coast that the storm impacted.

assessments.srl: Keeps the full Alaskan coast phrase as ARG1; the qualifier is not separately compiled.
assessments.amr: The input graph has coast :part-of state named Alaskan. Normalization reverses the edge; the current compiler lists it as untranslated and does not enforce it. Partial output, not faithful full compilation.
assessments.direct: Attaches Alaskan as a modifier of coast. This attachment is carried into a property atom.
assessments.guided: Attaches alaskan to coast; extra determiner concepts show that the representation is less canonical than pretrained AMR.

cases.title: Name fidelity and nested noun phrases
cases.requirement: Retain the phrase Phillies fan son without silently rewriting the team or dropping son. The noun-phrase relationship itself needs review.

assessments.srl: Preserves the exact phrase and receive role; the son/fan relationship remains inside one argument phrase.
assessments.amr: Changes Phillies to Phillips. The output is valid and executable but the name is wrong.
assessments.direct: Drops son from the recipient description. This loses claim content even though compilation succeeds.
assessments.guided: Retains son/fan/Phillies concepts but treats an article as a semantic modifier. Internal noun-phrase semantics remain provisional.

cases.title: Unlicensed negation
cases.requirement: Was landing is past progressive; it does not mean did not land.

assessments.srl: Retains the lander and location and adds past/progressive from the source auxiliary sequence.
assessments.amr: Returns a positive landing graph. Source alignment distinguishes past/progressive from the other landing forms.
assessments.direct: Adds :polarity - without a negation in the source sentence. This is an incorrect accepted translation.
assessments.guided: Does not add negation, but its graph has repeated variable declarations and is refused. This is not a successful parse.

cases.title: Shared subject across events
cases.requirement: The same Alice hugs Bob and waves; two separate events share one participant.

assessments.srl: The trained SRL control output has no predicate with arguments; this route refuses the claim. No replacement parse was hand-written.
assessments.amr: The two event graphs share the Alice node. The compiler retains that shared variable across conjunction.
assessments.direct: Declares a repeatedly for different nodes; refused. The graph does not provide a usable shared-reference representation.
assessments.guided: The hug and wave frames share one Alice node. The compiler retains the shared subject.

cases.title: Positive perfect clause
cases.requirement: Buildings have collapsed is positive and perfect, with buildings as the collapse participant.

assessments.srl: Preserves a positive collapse frame; source alignment supplies present/perfect.
assessments.amr: collapse-01 ARG1=building, positive. Source alignment supplies present/perfect.
assessments.direct: Uses ARG0=building instead of collapse-01 ARG1. This is an incorrect role frame even though compilation succeeds.
assessments.guided: Adds negative polarity and ARG0=building to a positive sentence. This is an incorrect accepted translation.
